items.caption:
strawberries & cream tiramisu🍓✨

this is such an easy no bake summer dessert that you can pop in the fridge. let me know if you try it

RECIPE (save for later)

Shopping list
✨For the strawberry layers:
•500g fresh strawberries
•50g granulated sugar
•2 tbsp lemon juice

✨For the cream layers:
•300ml whipping cream 
•250g mascarpone
•60g icing sugar
•1 tsp vanilla extract
•24 sponge fingers (depending on the dish size)
•sliced strawberries and fresh mint to garnish

1️⃣Heat the strawberries and sugar to a pan and heat until soft. Blend the mixture until smooth

2️⃣Whip the cream, vanilla extract and icing sugar until soft peaks form and then mix in the mascarpone until smooth

3️⃣Lay the sponge fingers in a dish, pour over the strawberry sauce, add the cream, layer with strawberries and repeat

4️⃣Garnish with strawberries, fresh mint or any fruit of your choice

5️⃣Pop in the fridge for a couple of hours or overnight if possible so that the sponge fingers can soak up the flavours.
items.transcript: This strawberries and cream tiramisu is the perfect, easy, no-bake summer dessert. Technically, it's not really a tiramisu because it doesn't contain coffee, just plenty of sweet, juicy strawberries with sponge fingers layered with thick whipped cream mixed with mascarpone. Hosting is my love language, and although I'm not the best at cooking, making food for my family and friends really brings me joy. It doesn't need to be anything fancy. This was so easy to make and everyone seemed to enjoy it.

items.caption:
tips for decluttering & organising your freezer✨

❄️create your own little supermarket by grouping items together - meat, fish, ready meals, vegetables, fruit, ice creams & desserts.

❄️write a list on your phone with an inventory of the items in your freezer.

❄️remove any items that have been lurking in the freezer for too long. 

❄️the recommended storage times for freezing items to keep their quality are:

raw chicken (9 months)
raw beef (6-12 months)
raw minced beef (4-6 months)
raw pork (4-6 months)
bacon & sausages (1-2 months)
raw fish (6-8 months)
raw oily fish (2-3 months)
cooked meat (2-3 months)

bread (3 months)
cheese (6 months)
milk (1 month)
ice cream (2 months)

vegetables (8-12 months)
herbs (6 months)
fruit (8-12 months)

#deepcleaning #cleanwithme #satisfyingcleaning #homeorganisation
items.transcript: I've never decluttered my freezer, so it was no surprise that I found items that expired in 2022. I'm not really sure why I decided that during a heatwave was a sensible time to do this job, but I probably shouldn't recommend it. But it actually was a good way of keeping cool for half an hour. I was fed up of not knowing what was in the freezer. The drawers were jam-packed and quite a few strange chips and peas in the bottom of the drawers. I'm really trying to lock in and get organised with my meal planning, so I've written a list of everything we've got in the freezer now. My top tip is to treat your freezer like your own little supermarket, grouping all the similar products together. I use the grab and go method, so basically you should be able to grab every item easily, rather than it being like an arctic treasure hunt every time you need some frozen chips.
